summary: This is documentation for a Terminal component—a reusable React UI element that displays styled terminal/console output on Docusaurus pages. It supports customizable titles, optional typewriter animation where commands appear character-by-character, and can load content from external files or inline JSX. The component is designed to make CLI examples visually appealing and interactive.

explanations.11: The typewriter animation feature makes command lines (starting with $ or #) appear one character at a time, while output lines show up all at once—mimicking how a real terminal would display them.
explanations.46: The `source` prop lets you point to an external text file instead of writing terminal content directly in your code; a build-time plugin automatically reads and injects that file's contents.
explanations.50: If you don't specify `typewriterSpeed`, the component automatically picks a speed based on how many lines you have—fewer lines get slower typing (more dramatic), many lines get faster typing (less tedious).
explanations.97: Lines beginning with `$` or `>` are recognized as shell commands and get a visual prompt marker to make them stand out from regular output.
explanations.121: When you use template literals (backticks) in JSX, you need to escape the `$` with a backslash so JavaScript doesn't try to interpret `${something}` as a variable placeholder instead of literal text.
